answer_text:
Let  

\[
D=\min_{i\neq j}\|x_i-x_j\|.
\]

We will show that \(D\le \sqrt2\), and then exhibit a configuration attaining equality.

---

### 1. Upper bound: \(D\le \sqrt2\)

Suppose, for contradiction, that all six pairwise distances are strictly larger than \(\sqrt2\). For two unit vectors \(x_i,x_j\),

\[
\|x_i-x_j\|^2
= \|x_i\|^2+\|x_j\|^2-2x_i\cdot x_j
=2-2x_i\cdot x_j.
\]

Thus \(\|x_i-x_j\|>\sqrt2\) implies

\[
2-2x_i\cdot x_j>2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
x_i\cdot x_j<0.
\]

So if \(D>\sqrt2\), then every pair of distinct points has negative dot product.

Now consider any five of the six points, say \(x_1,\dots,x_5\). The five vectors

\[
(x_1,1),\dots,(x_5,1)\in \mathbb R^4
\]

are linearly dependent, so there exist real numbers \(a_1,\dots,a_5\), not all zero, such that

\[
\sum_{i=1}^5 a_i x_i=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^5 a_i=0.
\]

Because the coefficients sum to zero, some are positive and some are negative. Let

\[
P=\{i:a_i>0\},\qquad N=\{i:a_i<0\}.
\]

Then both \(P\) and \(N\) are nonempty, and

\[
\sum_{i\in P}a_i x_i=-\sum_{j\in N}a_j x_j=:w.
\]

Taking the squared norm of \(w\), we get

\[
\|w\|^2
=
\left\langle \sum_{i\in P}a_i x_i,\; -\sum_{j\in N}a_j x_j\right\rangle
=
\sum_{i\in P}\sum_{j\in N} a_i(-a_j)(x_i\cdot x_j).
\]

For every \(i\in P\) and \(j\in N\), we have \(i\neq j\), \(a_i>0\), \(-a_j>0\), and by assumption \(x_i\cdot x_j<0\). Hence every term in the double sum is strictly negative, so

\[
\|w\|^2<0,
\]

which is impossible. Therefore our assumption was false, and among any six points on \(S^2\) there must be at least one pair with distance at most \(\sqrt2\). Hence

\[
M_6\le \sqrt2.
\]

---

### 2. Construction attaining \(\sqrt2\)

Take the six vertices of a regular octahedron:

\[
(\pm 1,0,0),\quad (0,\pm 1,0),\quad (0,0,\pm 1).
\]

All lie on the unit sphere. Distances between opposite points are \(2\), while distances between points on different coordinate axes are

\[
\sqrt{(1-0)^2+(0-1)^2+0^2}=\sqrt2.
\]

Thus the minimum pairwise distance is exactly \(\sqrt2\).

---

Combining the upper bound and the construction,

\[
M_6=\boxed{\sqrt2}.
\]
